concepts.title: Direction Cosines and Their Identity
concepts.definition: The cosines of the angles a directed line makes with the positive x, y and z axes are its direction cosines; their squares always total one, and any proportional triple of numbers serves as direction ratios.
concepts.formula: l**2 + m**2 + n**2 = 1 for direction cosines l, m, n
concepts.key_idea: Direction cosines carry the line's orientation and satisfy a unit-square identity.

concepts.title: Direction Cosines of the Line Through Two Points
concepts.definition: For the line joining two points, each direction cosine equals the corresponding coordinate difference divided by the distance between the points; the differences themselves are direction ratios.
concepts.formula: direction cosines = (x2 - x1)/pq_dist, (y2 - y1)/pq_dist, (z2 - z1)/pq_dist where pq_dist is the point separation
concepts.key_idea: Difference the coordinates, then divide each difference by the separation.

concepts.title: Cartesian Equation of a Line from Direction Ratios
concepts.definition: In coordinates the same line reads as three equal ratios: each coordinate minus its anchor value, divided by the matching direction ratio; unequal zero components drop their fraction and become separate equations.
concepts.key_idea: Equal ratios of shifted coordinates over direction numbers encode the line.

concepts.title: Cosine of the Angle Between Two Lines
concepts.definition: The acute angle between two lines is computed from their direction vectors exactly as for vectors: the dot product divided by the product of the magnitudes gives the cosine of the angle.
concepts.key_idea: Angle between lines reduces to angle between their direction vectors.

concepts.title: Perpendicular and Parallel Lines from Direction Ratios
concepts.definition: Two lines are perpendicular exactly when the dot product of their direction ratios vanishes, and parallel exactly when their direction ratios are proportional; both tests are component checks.
concepts.key_idea: Dot zero means right angle; proportional ratios mean parallel lines.

concepts.title: Shortest Distance Between Two Skew Lines
concepts.definition: Skew lines share no plane, so a unique segment meets both at right angles; its length equals the absolute value of the join of the two anchor points dotted with the unit normal obtained from the cross product of the two direction vectors.
concepts.formula: skew distance = abs(join_vector . (b1_vector x b2_vector)) / magnitude(b1_vector x b2_vector)
concepts.key_idea: Project the anchor-to-anchor join onto the common perpendicular direction.

concepts.title: Distance Between Two Parallel Lines
concepts.definition: Parallel lines are coplanar, and the distance between them is the length of the perpendicular from a point of one line to the other; it equals the magnitude of the cross product of the direction vector with the join of the two anchor points, divided by the direction magnitude.
concepts.formula: parallel distance = magnitude(b_vector x join_vector) / magnitude(b_vector)
concepts.key_idea: Cross the direction with the anchor join, then normalise by the direction length.
